docs.title: Aurastream
docs.text:
One endpoint. 37 data sources. Zero infrastructure.

Aurastream is a unified financial data API. Instead of integrating with each exchange and data provider individually, make a single POST request to Aurastream and get OHLCV bars, trades, quotes, funding rates, economic indicators, and more.

docs.title: Why Aurastream?
docs.text: Without Aurastream With Aurastream Integrate each exchange API separately One POST request for all sources Handle each provider's rate limits, pagination, retries Handled server-side Run infrastructure to host data pipelines We host it for you Different response formats per provider Consistent {ticker: {timestamp: {OHLCV}}}

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Errors come back as an HTTP status code with a JSON body containing a message.

Status Body (example) Cause Retry? 400 Bad Request {"message": "..."} Invalid parameters: unknown source, bad date format, unsupported interval, missing credentials for a source that needs them No: fix the request 403 Forbidden {"message": "Forbidden"} Missing or invalid x-api-key header, the key was deleted (for example after cancelling a plan), or it is paused because a renewal payment failed (see Billing) No: check the key and your subscription in the dashboard 429 Too Many Requests {"message": "Limit Exceeded"} Monthly allowance for your plan is used up After the monthly reset, or upgrade. See Plans & Limits 429 Too Many Requests {"message": "Too Many Requests"} Requests sent faster than your plan's rate Yes, after a short pause 500 Internal Server Error {"message": "..."} The upstream data source failed or returned an error Yes, with backoff 504 Gateway Timeout {"message": "Endpoint request timed out"} The request took too long, usually a very large range or many tickers Yes, after splitting the request

docs.title: Retrying safely
docs.text:
Retry only 429 Too Many Requests (rate), 500 and 504. Wait between attempts and increase the wait each time:

import time
import requests

def fetch(payload, retries=4):
    for attempt in range(retries):
        r = requests.post(URL, headers=HEADERS, json=payload, timeout=130)
        if r.status_code == 200:
            return r.json()
        if r.status_code == 429 and r.json().get("message") == "Limit Exceeded":
            raise RuntimeError("Monthly allowance used up")
        if r.status_code in (429, 500, 504):
            time.sleep(2 ** attempt)
            continue
        r.raise_for_status()
    r.raise_for_status()

Don't retry 400 or 403: the same request will fail again.

docs.title: Response Format
docs.text: All successful responses from the /timeseries endpoint return data in the same nested dictionary format, regardless of the data source.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text: {ticker: {timestamp: {field: value}}}

docs.title: Single ticker
docs.text:
import pandas as pd

ticker = "EUR_USD"
df = pd.DataFrame.from_dict(data[ticker], orient="index")
df.index = pd.to_datetime(df.index)
df = df.astype(float).sort_index()

docs.title: Multiple tickers
docs.text:
frames = {}
for ticker, values in data.items():
    df = pd.DataFrame.from_dict(values, orient="index")
    df.index = pd.to_datetime(df.index)
    frames[ticker] = df.astype(float).sort_index()

# Access individual DataFrames
eur = frames["EUR_USD"]
gbp = frames["GBP_USD"]

docs.title: Multi-level DataFrame
docs.text:
panels = []
for ticker, values in data.items():
    df = pd.DataFrame.from_dict(values, orient="index")
    df.index = pd.to_datetime(df.index)
    df = df.astype(float).sort_index()
    df.columns = pd.MultiIndex.from_product([[ticker], df.columns])
    panels.append(df)

combined = pd.concat(panels, axis=1)
# Access: combined["EUR_USD"]["Close"]

docs.title: Extracting a Single Field
docs.text:
To pull just the closing prices for plotting or analysis:

def to_series(data, ticker, field="Close"):
    ts = data[ticker]
    s = pd.Series({k: float(v[field]) for k, v in ts.items()})
    s.index = pd.to_datetime(s.index)
    return s.sort_index()

close = to_series(data, "EUR_USD", "Close")

docs.title: Empty Responses
docs.text:
If a ticker has no data for the requested range, its entry will be an empty dictionary:

{
    "INVALID_TICKER": {}
}

Check for this before processing:

if not data.get("INVALID_TICKER"):
    print("No data returned for this ticker")

docs.title: POST /timeseries
docs.text: Fetch historical time series data from any supported source.

docs.title: Endpoint
docs.text: POST https://api.aurastream.unbiased-alpha.com/timeseries

docs.title: Headers
docs.text: Header Required Description x-api-key Yes Your Aurastream API key Content-Type Yes application/json

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text:
{
    "tickerlist": ["BTCUSDT", "ETHUSDT"],
    "start": "2025-01-01",
    "end": "2025-06-01",
    "interval": "1d",
    "source": "bybit",
    "credentials": null
}

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description tickerlist list[str] Yes — List of ticker symbols to fetch start str Yes — Start date in YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM format, UTC end str Yes — End date in YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM format, UTC interval str Yes — Bar interval (see Intervals) source str Yes — Data source identifier (see Data Sources) credentials dict or null No null Source-specific credentials (see Credentials)

docs.title: Source-Specific Parameters
docs.text:
Any other field in the body is passed to the source. Sources ignore fields they don't use.

Parameter Used by Values (default first) dtype Alpaca "bars", "trades", "quotes" dtype Oanda "bars", "orderbook", "positionbook" dtype Yahoo Finance "candles", "earnings" price_type Oanda "M" (mid), "A" (ask), "B" (bid) assetclass Alpaca "equity", "crypto" feed Alpaca "iex", "sip" adjustment Alpaca "raw", "split", "dividend", "all" instrument Binance "spot", "futures" instrument Kraken "futures", "spot" bars Binance "candles", "funding" (futures only) bars FRED not set (series IDs), "cpi", "gdp", "3mrate", "10yrate" category Bybit "linear", "inverse" as_of FRED "realtime_start", "date" as_of CFTC "release", "report" dataset SEC EDGAR "insider", "financials", "earnings", "ftd", "13f"

docs.title: Intervals
docs.text:
The interval parameter accepts these formats:

Interval Meaning Examples 1s, 5s, 30s Seconds Polygon, Binance spot (1s only) 1M, 5M, 15M, 30M Minutes Most sources 1h, 4h Hours Most sources 1d Daily All sources 1w Weekly Most sources 1m Monthly Some sources

Case matters

Upper-case M is minutes, lower-case m is months: 15M is 15 minutes, 1m is one month.

Interval support varies by source

Not every source supports every interval. See individual data source pages for supported intervals.

docs.text:
Most price sources return bars by default. Other data types:

Data How to request it Source Individual trades "dtype": "trades" Alpaca Bid/ask quotes "dtype": "quotes" Alpaca Funding rates "bars": "funding", "instrument": "futures" Binance Order book snapshots (every 20 minutes) "dtype": "orderbook" Oanda Position book snapshots (every 20 minutes) "dtype": "positionbook" Oanda Earnings dates and EPS "dtype": "earnings" Yahoo Finance

docs.title: Alpaca
docs.text: US equities and crypto market data from Alpaca Markets.

docs.title: Source ID
docs.text: "source": "alpaca"

docs.title: Credentials
docs.text:
"credentials": {
    "key": "your-alpaca-api-key",
    "secret": "your-alpaca-secret-key"
}

Get your credentials at Alpaca.

docs.title: Ticker Format
docs.text:
US equity symbols, and slash-separated pairs for crypto (with "assetclass": "crypto"):

Example Instrument AAPL Apple Inc. MSFT Microsoft Corp. SPY S&P 500 ETF BTC/USD Bitcoin (crypto) ETH/USD Ethereum (crypto) BTC/USDT Bitcoin / Tether (crypto)

docs.title: Supported Intervals
docs.text:
1M, 1h, 1d, 1w, 1m

Only single units are used: the number in front is ignored, so 15M returns 1-minute bars. Resample on your side for other bar sizes.

Bar fields: open, high, low, close, volume, trade_count, vwap.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Values Default Description dtype "bars", "trades", "quotes" "bars" Data type assetclass "equity", "crypto" "equity" Asset class feed "iex", "sip" "iex" Stocks only. "iex" is IEX trades only (thin volume, and for most names no history before mid-2020). "sip" is the consolidated tape from 2016; historical SIP data works on any Alpaca account, only the last 15 minutes need a subscription, so AuraStream stops SIP requests 16 minutes before now adjustment "raw", "split", "dividend", "all" "raw" Stock bars only: as traded, or adjusted for splits, dividends or both

Rate limits

Alpaca allows 200 API calls per minute. Aurastream retries rate-limited calls (HTTP 429) with exponential backoff; other errors, such as an unknown symbol, come back at once. Large ticker lists are batched (50 per request by default).

docs.title: BEA National Accounts
docs.text:
US personal consumption expenditures (PCE), the PCE price index (the Fed's inflation gauge), personal income and saving, and GDP, from the Bureau of Economic Analysis.

Source: bea | Credentials: Required (free key)

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
    "tickerlist": ["pce", "pce_real", "core_pce_price", "saving_rate"],
    "start": "2023-01-01",
    "end": "2026-12-31",
    "interval": "1m",
    "source": "bea",
    "credentials": {
        "api_key": "YOUR_BEA_KEY"
    }
}

docs.title: Ticker Format
docs.text:
A name below, or any line of a BEA national accounts (NIPA) table as <table>:<line>, e.g. T20805:3. Table names and line numbers are in BEA's interactive tables.

Ticker Series Frequency pce Personal consumption expenditures, current dollars, seasonally adjusted annual rate Monthly pce_goods, pce_durables, pce_nondurables, pce_services PCE by type of product Monthly pce_real Real PCE, chained dollars Monthly pce_price, core_pce_price PCE price index; excluding food and energy Monthly personal_income, disposable_income Personal income; disposable personal income Monthly saving_rate Personal saving as a percent of disposable income Monthly gdp GDP, current dollars, seasonally adjusted annual rate Quarterly gdp_real_growth Real GDP, percent change at an annual rate Quarterly

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description frequency str No "M", "Q" or "A"; default is the series' own (monthly, or quarterly for GDP). Use it for <table>:<line> tickers from quarterly or annual tables

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
One row per period, stamped at the first day of the month, quarter or year:

Field Description value Value as BEA publishes it unit BEA's unit, e.g. Level or Percent unit_mult Power of ten the value is expressed in: 6 = millions of dollars (PCE, income, GDP), 0 = as is (indexes, percentages) line BEA's description of the line

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Values are the latest estimates. BEA revises recent months with each release and older data in its annual updates, so these are not the figures first published. econcalendar (bea) gives the release times.
  • PCE for a month is published at the end of the following month (Personal Income and Outlays release); GDP about a month after the quarter.
  • BEA allows 100 requests a minute per key.
  • This product uses the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) Data API but is not endorsed or certified by BEA.

docs.title: CFTC Commitments of Traders
docs.text: Weekly positioning in US futures markets from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission: who holds each contract (hedgers, swap dealers, hedge funds, small traders), back to 2006.

docs.title: Source ID
docs.text: "source": "cftc"

docs.title: Credentials
docs.text: Not required.

docs.title: Ticker Format
docs.text:
Common futures symbols, or any CFTC contract market code:

Example Market GC, SI, HG, PL, PA Gold, silver, copper, platinum, palladium CL, NG, RB, HO Crude oil, natural gas, gasoline, heating oil ZC, ZS, ZW Corn, soybeans, wheat KC, SB, CC Coffee, sugar, cocoa LE, HE Live cattle, lean hogs YM, RTY, VX Dow, Russell 2000, VIX futures ZT, ZF, ZN, ZB, SR3 Treasury futures, SOFR 6E, 6J, 6B, 6A, 6C, 6S, 6M, DX Currency futures, dollar index BTC, ETH CME crypto futures 088691 Any CFTC contract market code

Any other symbol is sent to the CFTC as a contract market code.

docs.title: Timing
docs.text: Positions are as of Tuesday and published Friday at 15:30 New York. By default each report is stamped at its publication time (in UTC), so it can be used in backtests without look-ahead. The original Tuesday date is in the report_date field. In holiday weeks the CFTC publishes a day or two later than this rule.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Each row carries every numeric column of the chosen report (long, short and spread positions by trader group, changes, percentages of open interest, trader counts) under the CFTC's own column names, plus report_date. The interval parameter is ignored: the data is weekly.

docs.title: Parameters

Source: edgar | Credentials: Contact string required by the SEC

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description dataset str No "insider" (default, Form 4 trades), "financials" (reported figures), "earnings" (earnings release filings), "ftd" (fails-to-deliver), "13f" (institutional holdings) or "nport" (fund holdings) concepts list[str] No XBRL concepts for financials, e.g. ["Revenues", "CostOfGoldProductsAndServices"]. Default: revenue, costs, income, EPS, cash flow, capex, cash, debt, equity, shares period str No "quarter" (default) or "annual" for financials top int No nport only: keep the largest N positions of each filing (default: all)

docs.title: Ticker Format
docs.text:
US stock symbols (AAPL) or SEC CIK numbers (320193, 1164727 for Newmont).

  • ftd: a symbol (GME) or a 9-character CUSIP.
  • 13f: the manager's CIK, e.g. 1067983 for Berkshire Hathaway. Find a manager's CIK with EDGAR company search.
  • nport: a mutual fund or ETF ticker (VTSAX, IVV, ARKK, SPY), or the fund's SEC series id (S000002848).

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
insider: one row per Form 4 filing, stamped when it became public (SEC acceptance time):

Field Description owner, officer_title Who filed is_director, is_officer, is_ten_percent_owner Relationship to the company (1/0) buy_shares, buy_value Open-market purchases (code P) sell_shares, sell_value Open-market sales (code S) other_shares_net Net shares from grants, option exercises, gifts plan_10b5_1 1 if the trades were under a pre-arranged 10b5-1 plan shares_owned_after, transaction_date, n_transactions Holdings afterwards, first trade date, number of trades

financials: one row per filing date, with each concept's value and its calendar period (e.g. Revenues, Revenues_period: "CY2024Q2").

earnings: one row per 8-K filing that reports results of operations (item 2.02), stamped when it became public. This is when a company's earnings release reached the SEC, usually minutes after the press release:

Field Description event_date Date of the event the 8-K reports (usually the release date) items All 8-K items in the filing, e.g. 2.02,9.01 form, accession, url Filing type (8-K or 8-K/A), SEC accession number, link to the document

ftd: fails-to-deliver, one row per settlement date on which the stock had fails outstanding at the NSCC (aggregated over all clearing members):

Field Description fails Total fails-to-deliver balance, in shares price Previous day's closing price symbol, cusip, description Security

13f: one row per 13F-HR filing (and amendments), stamped when it became public:

Field Description report_period Quarter end the holdings refer to n_positions, total_value Number of positions and their total value holdings List of positions: issuer, class, cusip, value, shares, share_type (SH shares or PRN principal), put_call, discretion form, accession 13F-HR or 13F-HR/A, SEC accession number

nport: one row per Form N-PORT filing (and amendments), stamped when it became public:

Field Description fund, series_id, report_period Fund name, SEC series id, month end the holdings refer to total_assets, net_assets In US dollars flow_sales, flow_redemptions, flow_reinvestment Money in (shares sold), out (redeemed) and dividends reinvested over the three months of the quarter, in US dollars returns_pct Total returns of the ticker's share class for the three months, in percent n_holdings Number of positions in the filing holdings List of positions, largest first: name, title, cusip, isin, ticker (when the fund reports one), lei, balance, units (NS shares, PA principal, NC contracts), currency, value_usd, pct_net_assets (percent), payoff (Long/Short), asset_cat (EC equity, DBT debt, ...), issuer_cat, country form, accession NPORT-P or NPORT-P/A, SEC accession number

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The SEC requires automated requests to identify the sender with a name and contact email; no registration is needed.
  • Requests are throttled to the SEC limit of 10 per second, so long insider ranges for very active companies take a while.
  • ftd data is published twice a month, for the first and second half of each month, about two weeks after the period ends. Rows are stamped at the settlement date, so recent dates appear late.
  • 13f filings are due 45 days after each quarter end. value is in US dollars for filings from 2023; earlier filings reported thousands of dollars. Large managers file thousands of positions: request a year or less at a time.
  • nport: funds report every month, but only the last month of each fiscal quarter is made public, about 60 days after it ends. Data from late 2019. A fund with thousands of positions (a total market index fund) returns about 5 MB a year: use top or a shorter range to stay under the 10 MB response limit. Money market funds file a different form and are not included.
  • All EDGAR content is free to reuse (SEC policy).

docs.title: Response Format
docs.text:
FRED values get revised. AuraStream returns every published version, so you can see what was known at any point in time. Rows hold a list called updates rather than OHLC fields.

With the default as_of: "realtime_start", each row is a publication date and lists the values published that day, with the period they refer to:

{
    "CPIAUCSL": {
        "2025-02-12 00:00:00": {
            "updates": [
                {"reference_date": "2025-01-01 00:00:00", "value": 317.671}
            ]
        }
    }
}

This is the version to use in backtests: a row only contains what was public on that date. start and end filter on the publication date.

With as_of: "date", each row is the period the value describes and lists every version published for it, with publication_date in place of reference_date.

import pandas as pd

data = response.json()
rows = []
for published, row in data["US"].items():
    for u in row["updates"]:
        rows.append({"published": published, "period": u["reference_date"], "value": u["value"]})

docs.title: Choosing a Source
docs.text:
Forex & Metals: Use oanda with your own account for bid, ask and mid bars and Oanda's order and position books, or yahoo without an account.

Crypto: Use binance, bybit or kraken for exchange-native bars without credentials; binance also has funding rates, deribit covers options and kucoin its futures and indices. For on-chain perpetuals use hyperliquid or dydx; coinapi and coingecko cover many more exchanges and coins with your own key.

US Equities: Use alpaca or polygon with your own account for intraday bars, trades and quotes, or yahoo without an account.

Futures History: Use firstrate with your FirstRate Data account for long intraday histories of continuous or individual futures contracts.

Economic Data: Use fred for macro indicators across many countries, and sdmx for series published by central banks and statistics agencies. econcalendar gives the scheduled release times of the main US figures and FOMC decisions.

Company Fundamentals: Use finnhub for company metrics, and edgar for financials as reported to the SEC and the times earnings releases were filed.

Positioning & Flows: Use cftc for who holds each futures market, and edgar for insider purchases and sales, fails-to-deliver, institutional (13F) holdings, and mutual fund and ETF holdings and flows (nport).

Energy & Liquidity: Use eia for oil and gas inventories, and treasury for government cash and auctions, which drive dollar liquidity.

Metals & Trade Flows: Use hmrc, comext, uscensus and hktrade for gold, silver and base-metal shipments between countries (e.g. gold:CH), and worldbank for long monthly price histories.

Crypto Fundamentals & News: Use defillama for stablecoin supply and DeFi activity, and gdelt for news coverage and tone on any topic.

Consumer Activity: Use uscensus (dataset: "retail") for monthly retail sales by store type, bea for personal consumption expenditures, income and saving, and tsa for daily US air travel. Consumer credit (Federal Reserve G.19) is in fred (TOTALSL, REVOLSL, NONREVSL). econcalendar gives the release times.

docs.title: Macro Analysis Example
docs.text: This example replicates a real macro analysis: comparing oil prices, commodity-linked currencies, and the dollar index to visualize how macro forces connect.

docs.title: The Setup
docs.text:
We fetch data from multiple sources to build a cross-asset view:

  • Brent Crude Oil from Yahoo Finance
  • USD/NOK (oil-linked currency) from Oanda
  • USD/BRL (commodity-linked currency) from Yahoo Finance
  • Dollar Index (DXY) from Yahoo Finance

docs.title: Full Code
docs.text:
import requests
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

URL = "https://api.aurastream.unbiased-alpha.com/timeseries"
HEADERS = {"x-api-key": "YOUR_AURASTREAM_API_KEY"}


def to_series(data, ticker, field="Close"):
    """Extract closing prices as a pandas Series."""
    ts = data[ticker]
    s = pd.Series({k: float(v[field]) for k, v in ts.items()})
    s.index = pd.to_datetime(s.index).normalize()
    return s.sort_index()


# --- 1. Oil (Brent Crude) from Yahoo ---
oil = requests.post(URL, headers=HEADERS, json={
    "tickerlist": ["BZ=F"],
    "start": "2025-01-01",
    "end": "2026-07-01",
    "interval": "1d",
    "source": "yahoo",
}).json()

# --- 2. USD/NOK from Oanda (requires credentials) ---
fx_nok = requests.post(URL, headers=HEADERS, json={
    "tickerlist": ["USD_NOK"],
    "start": "2025-01-01",
    "end": "2026-07-01",
    "interval": "1d",
    "source": "oanda",
    "price_type": "A",
    "credentials": {
        "id": "YOUR_OANDA_ACCOUNT_ID",
        "token": "YOUR_OANDA_TOKEN",
        "environment": "practice"
    }
}).json()

# --- 3. USD/BRL from Yahoo ---
fx_brl = requests.post(URL, headers=HEADERS, json={
    "tickerlist": ["BRL=X"],
    "start": "2025-01-01",
    "end": "2026-07-01",
    "interval": "1d",
    "source": "yahoo",
}).json()

# --- 4. Dollar Index (DXY) from Yahoo ---
dxy = requests.post(URL, headers=HEADERS, json={
    "tickerlist": ["DX-Y.NYB"],
    "start": "2025-01-01",
    "end": "2026-07-01",
    "interval": "1d",
    "source": "yahoo",
}).json()


# --- Build normalized comparison ---
brent  = to_series(oil,    "BZ=F")
usdnok = to_series(fx_nok, "USD_NOK")
usdbrl = to_series(fx_brl, "BRL=X")
dollar = to_series(dxy,    "DX-Y.NYB")

# Normalize: percentage change from start date
norm = pd.DataFrame({
    "Brent Crude":  brent  / brent.iloc[0]  * 100 - 100,
    "USD/NOK":      usdnok / usdnok.iloc[0] * 100 - 100,
    "USD/BRL":      usdbrl / usdbrl.iloc[0]  * 100 - 100,
    "Dollar Index": dollar / dollar.iloc[0]  * 100 - 100,
}).ffill()


# --- Plot ---
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 6))
norm.plot(ax=ax, linewidth=1.8)
ax.set_title("Three stories. One macro picture.", fontsize=16, fontweight="bold")
ax.set_ylabel("% change from Jan 2025")
ax.axhline(0, color="grey", linewidth=0.5, linestyle="--")
ax.legend(loc="best", fontsize=11)
ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("aurastream_macro.png", dpi=150)
plt.show()

docs.title: What This Shows
docs.text:
Normalizing each series to percentage change from a common start date puts them on one scale, so you can check:

  • whether oil and the oil-linked currencies (NOK, BRL) move together over the period
  • how the dollar index moves against commodity prices
  • how much larger the moves in an emerging-market currency (BRL) are

Each source is one request and returns the same {ticker: {timestamp: {field: value}}} shape. Daily bars are stamped at different times of day by different sources (Yahoo at midnight New York in UTC, Oanda at the bar close), which is why to_series normalizes the index to the date.

docs.title: Adding Inflation from FRED
docs.text:
FRED rows hold every published version of a value rather than OHLC fields (see FRED). To line up US CPI with the prices above as it was known at the time, index it by publication date:

cpi = requests.post(URL, headers=HEADERS, json={
    "tickerlist": ["CPIAUCSL"],
    "start": "2025-01-01",
    "end": "2026-07-01",
    "interval": "1m",
    "source": "fred",
    "credentials": {"key": "YOUR_FRED_KEY"}
}).json()

# One row per publication date; keep the newest period released that day
released = pd.Series({
    pd.Timestamp(published).normalize(): max(row["updates"], key=lambda u: u["reference_date"])["value"]
    for published, row in cpi["CPIAUCSL"].items()
}).sort_index()

norm["US CPI (as released)"] = (released / released.iloc[0] * 100 - 100).reindex(norm.index, method="ffill")
# then run the plot block again

def to_dataframe(data, ticker):
    """Convert Aurastream response to a pandas DataFrame."""
    df = pd.DataFrame.from_dict(data[ticker], orient="index")

    s.index = pd.to_datetime(s.index)
    return s.sort_index()

docs.text:
Aurastream uses two layers of authentication:

  1. Aurastream API key — authenticates you against the Aurastream service
  2. Data source credentials — your own credentials for third-party data providers (when required)

docs.title: Aurastream API Key
docs.text:
Every request must include your Aurastream API key in the x-api-key header:

headers = {"x-api-key": "YOUR_AURASTREAM_API_KEY"}

You can find your API key in the Aurastream dashboard under API Keys.

Keep your API key secret

Never commit your API key to version control or share it publicly. Use environment variables or a secrets manager.

import os

headers = {"x-api-key": os.environ["AURASTREAM_API_KEY"]}

docs.title: Data Source Credentials
docs.text:
Some data sources require your own API credentials to access their data. These are passed in the credentials field of the request body — they are not stored on Aurastream servers.

response = requests.post(URL, headers=headers, json={
    "tickerlist": ["EUR_USD"],
    "start": "2025-01-01",
    "end": "2025-06-01",
    "interval": "1h",
    "source": "oanda",
    "credentials": {
        "id": "YOUR_OANDA_ACCOUNT_ID",
        "token": "YOUR_OANDA_TOKEN",
        "environment": "practice"
    }
})

Credentials are never stored

Aurastream uses your credentials only to call the upstream data source for your request. They are not saved to your account.

docs.title: Which sources need credentials?
docs.text:
Source Credentials Required Notes Oanda Yes Account ID + API token Alpaca Yes API key + secret Polygon Yes API key FRED Yes API key Finnhub Yes API key EIA Yes API key (free) US Census Yes API key (free) BEA Yes API key (free) SEC EDGAR Yes Name and contact email, no registration US Economic Calendar (bls) Yes Name and contact email, no registration; other agencies need none Binance No Public market data Bybit No Public market data Kraken No Public market data Yahoo Finance No Public data CFTC, US Treasury, DefiLlama, TSA No Public data GDELT, World Bank, UK Trade (HMRC), EU Trade (Eurostat), Hong Kong Trade No Public data

See the Credentials guide for the exact format each source expects.

docs.title: Free plan
docs.text: The Free plan never charges you and never asks for a card. It renews automatically each month.

docs.title: Trials
docs.text: Some paid plans start with a free trial. You need a card on file to start one, and each account can use one trial. When the trial ends, the plan renews automatically and your card is charged, unless you cancel before the end date shown in the dashboard.

docs.title: Renewals
docs.text: Paid plans renew automatically at the end of each billing period (monthly or yearly), charging your default card. You get an email with the invoice after each successful payment. You can switch auto-renewal off, or change between monthly and yearly billing, in the dashboard.

docs.title: If a payment fails
docs.text:
If a renewal can't be charged, your subscription is put on hold, your API keys stop working (requests return 403 Forbidden), and you get an email. This happens when:

  • the card is declined or expired, or
  • your bank requires an extra confirmation step (such as 3-D Secure), which can't be completed for automatic renewals.

We retry the charge once a day using your current default card. To restore access straight away, update your card under Payment Methods, then open Manage Subscription and click Renew Subscription. Your existing keys start working again as soon as the payment goes through.

If the payment still hasn't gone through 7 days after the renewal date, the subscription is cancelled and its keys are deleted. You can subscribe again at any time, including on the free plan.

docs.title: Cancelling
docs.text: Cancel any time from the dashboard. Cancelling deletes your API keys immediately, so requests with them will return 403 Forbidden.

docs.title: Credentials Reference
docs.text: Each data source that requires authentication expects a specific credential format in the credentials field of the request body.

docs.title: Public Sources (No Credentials Needed)
docs.text:
The following sources do not require credentials — omit the credentials field or pass null:

  • Binance — public spot and futures market data
  • Bybit — public perpetuals market data
  • Kraken — public spot and futures market data
  • Yahoo Finance — public equities, ETFs, indices, commodities
  • CFTC, US Treasury, DefiLlama — public positioning, fiscal and on-chain data
  • GDELT, World Bank, UK Trade (HMRC), EU Trade (Eurostat), Hong Kong Trade — public news and trade statistics
  • Deribit, KuCoin, Hyperliquid, dYdX, Derive (Lyra) — public crypto derivatives market data
  • SDMX, Open-Meteo — public statistical series and historical weather

docs.title: Claude & ChatGPT (MCP)
docs.text: The Aurastream MCP server lets AI assistants that support the Model Context Protocol (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, ChatGPT and others) fetch data from Aurastream themselves. You ask in plain language; the assistant picks the source, calls the /timeseries endpoint and works with the result.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
Tool Description list_sources Sources, asset classes, ticker formats, intervals, data types, and whether provider credentials are configured. Does not use your allowance. get_timeseries Calls /timeseries and returns a compact table per ticker: the most recent rows, 100 by default, up to 1000. get_latest The most recent N bars per ticker, without picking dates.

All 37 sources in Data Sources are available (version 0.1.2 or later):

Group Sources Crypto Binance, Bybit, Kraken, Deribit, KuCoin, dYdX, Hyperliquid, Derive; with your own key: CoinAPI; with a Nemeton subscription: Nemeton Equities, FX, futures, CFDs Yahoo Finance; with your own account: Oanda, Alpaca, Polygon, FirstRate, TradeStation, City Index Macro and energy US Treasury, World Bank, SDMX; with a free key: FRED, EIA; with your own key: Trading Economics, Nasdaq Data Link Fundamentals SEC EDGAR; with your own key: Finnhub Positioning and flows CFTC, UK Trade, EU Trade, Hong Kong Trade; with a free key: US Trade Crypto fundamentals and news DefiLlama, GDELT; with a free key: CoinGecko Weather Open-Meteo; with your own key: Visual Crossing

The server is open source (MIT): github.com/UnbiasedAlpha/aurastream-mcp.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
Requires Python 3.10+.

pip install aurastream-mcp

This installs the aurastream-mcp command. Check it with aurastream-mcp --help.

docs.title: 2. Configure your keys
docs.text:
The server reads every key from environment variables. Provider credentials are never typed into the chat and never pass through the model.

Variable Used for AURASTREAM_API_KEY Required. Your Aurastream key from the dashboard. OANDA_ACCOUNT_ID, OANDA_TOKEN Oanda OANDA_ENVIRONMENT Oanda, optional: practice (default) or live ALPACA_API_KEY, ALPACA_SECRET_KEY Alpaca POLYGON_API_KEY Polygon FRED_API_KEY FRED FINNHUB_API_KEY Finnhub FIRSTRATE_USER_ID FirstRate: the user ID FirstRate Data gives you for API downloads EIA_API_KEY EIA CENSUS_API_KEY US Trade EDGAR_USER_AGENT SEC EDGAR: your name and contact email, e.g. Your Company contact@yourcompany.com NEMETON_API_KEY Nemeton: the key from your Nemeton subscription COINAPI_KEY CoinAPI COINGECKO_API_KEY or COINGECKO_DEMO_API_KEY CoinGecko: a Pro key, or a free Demo key (last 365 days only) NASDAQ_DATA_LINK_API_KEY Nasdaq Data Link TRADINGECONOMICS_API_KEY Trading Economics TRADESTATION_CLIENT_ID, TRADESTATION_CLIENT_SECRET, TRADESTATION_REFRESH_TOKEN TradeStation CITYINDEX_USERNAME, CITYINDEX_PASSWORD, CITYINDEX_APP_KEY City Index VISUALCROSSING_API_KEY Visual Crossing OPENMETEO_API_KEY Open-Meteo, optional

The server turns these into the credentials object described in Credentials. Set only the ones you need.

docs.title: 3. Connect your assistant
4. Ask for data
docs.text:
Some prompts to try:

  • "What sources does Aurastream have for forex?"
  • "Get daily BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT from Binance for 2025 and compute their 30-day rolling correlation."
  • "Show the last 20 hourly bars of EUR_USD from Oanda."
  • "Show Binance BTCUSDT perpetual funding rates for June 2025."
  • "How has managed-money positioning in gold futures changed since 2020?"
  • "Show monthly UK gold exports to Switzerland since 2020."

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Historical data, not a real-time feed.
  • Each data request is one API call and counts against your monthly allowance (free plan: 500 calls per month, see Plans & Limits). When the allowance runs out the assistant is told so; it resets on the 1st.
  • Responses are capped per ticker so they fit in the assistant's context. For long, fine-grained histories, call the API directly.

docs.title: Plans & Limits
docs.text: Every API key belongs to a plan. The plan sets how many calls you can make per month and how fast you can make them.

docs.title: Free plan
docs.text:
Start without a card: every new account starts on Free. Sign up at the dashboard and your API key is ready under API Keys.

Free Price $0, no card needed API calls 500 per month Request rate 1 request per second (short bursts of up to 5) API keys 1 Data sources All sources in Data Sources

The monthly allowance resets on the 1st of each month (00:00 UTC). Unused calls don't carry over.

docs.title: Paid plans
docs.text:
Paid plans raise the monthly allowance and the request rate, and let you add more API keys. Current plans and prices are on the pricing page. Some paid plans start with a free trial; trials need a card on file.

To move from Free to a paid plan, choose the new plan on the pricing page in the dashboard. Once the payment (or trial) starts, the Free plan ends and you get a new API key on the new plan; the Free key stops working.

docs.title: What happens at the limit
docs.text:
When you go over a limit, the API answers with HTTP 429 instead of data:

Response body Meaning What to do {"message": "Limit Exceeded"} Monthly allowance used up Wait for the reset on the 1st, or upgrade {"message": "Too Many Requests"} Request rate too high Slow down and retry after a short pause

Calls rejected with 429 don't count against your allowance. See Errors for all error responses.

docs.title: Making the most of your calls
docs.text:
One call can return many tickers and a long date range, so batch your requests:

  • Put several tickers in one tickerlist instead of one call per ticker.
  • Request the whole date range you need in one call, then cache it locally.
  • Use the coarsest interval that works for your analysis.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: Get your first data in under 2 minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• An Aurastream API key: sign up at the dashboard: every new account starts on the Free plan (500 calls a month, no card needed) and the key is under API Keys
  • Python 3.8+ with requests installed, or any HTTP client

docs.title: 1. Install requests
docs.text: pip install requests

docs.title: 2. Make your first request
docs.text:
This example fetches daily Bitcoin data from Bybit (no exchange credentials needed):

import requests

URL = "https://api.aurastream.unbiased-alpha.com/timeseries"
HEADERS = {"x-api-key": "YOUR_AURASTREAM_API_KEY"}

response = requests.post(URL, headers=HEADERS, json={
    "tickerlist": ["BTCUSDT"],
    "start": "2025-06-01",
    "end": "2025-06-30",
    "interval": "1d",
    "source": "bybit",
})

data = response.json()
print(data)

docs.title: 3. Parse the response
docs.text:
The response is a nested dictionary: {ticker: {timestamp: {field: value}}}. Some sources, Bybit included, send prices as strings, hence the astype(float).

import pandas as pd

ticker = "BTCUSDT"
df = pd.DataFrame.from_dict(data[ticker], orient="index")
df.index = pd.to_datetime(df.index)
df = df.sort_index()
df = df.astype(float)

print(df.head())
#                  Open       High        Low      Close
# 2025-06-01  104636.10  105900.00  103900.50  105700.20
# 2025-06-02  105700.20  106200.00  104500.00  105400.00
# ...
# Bybit bars are built from the mark price, so there is no Volume column.

docs.title: 4. Try a source that requires credentials
docs.text:
Some sources (Oanda, Alpaca, etc.) require your own exchange credentials. Pass them in the request body:

response = requests.post(URL, headers=HEADERS, json={
    "tickerlist": ["EUR_USD", "GBP_USD"],
    "start": "2025-06-01",
    "end": "2025-06-30",
    "interval": "1h",
    "source": "oanda",
    "credentials": {
        "id": "YOUR_OANDA_ACCOUNT_ID",
        "token": "YOUR_OANDA_API_TOKEN",
        "environment": "practice"  # or "live"
    }
})
